title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

citations.claim: Van den Oord et al. introduced WaveNet, a deep autoregressive neural network that generates raw audio waveforms using stacks of dilated causal convolutions, achieving state-of-the-art text-to-speech naturalness.

WaveNet uses dilated causal convolutions with exponentially increasing dilation factors (1, 2, 4, ..., 512), enabling exponential receptive field growth with depth while preserving the input resolution and computational efficiency.
Van den Oord et al. employed gated activation units of the form z = tanh(W_f * x) . sigma(W_g * x), which significantly outperformed rectified linear activations for modeling audio signals.
WaveNet uses residual and skip connections throughout the network to speed up convergence and enable training of much deeper models.

WaveNet supports both global conditioning (e.g., speaker identity) and local conditioning (e.g., linguistic features) to guide audio generation, demonstrating that a single model can capture characteristics of over 100 speakers.

Van den Oord et al. showed that modeling audio sample distributions with a categorical softmax over mu-law quantized values works better than mixture density networks, because categorical distributions make no assumptions about distribution shape.
WaveNet reduced the gap in mean opinion score between the best synthetic speech and natural speech by more than 50% compared to prior parametric and concatenative systems.

The WaveNet architecture processes 1D sequences using stacks of dilated convolutions and has been widely adopted as a backbone for various audio and signal processing tasks beyond its original text-to-speech application.

do_not_claim: WaveNet was designed for or applied to signal separation or baseline correction
WaveNet uses algorithm unrolling or learned iterative optimization
WaveNet was applied to chromatographic data
